extra.message: patient_filebox_slot_010 writes files using attacker-controlled names: shelf.save(drop_blob.name, drop_blob) (uploaded filename) and shelf.save(packet_ref, ...) where packet_ref comes directly from request.GET. The filename is never sanitized, giving an attacker external control of the stored file path and allowing arbitrary file writes (and attempted path traversal via .. segments) inside the storage location.

patient_roster_fold_012 has no authentication and no _wrk_gate check (unlike peer ops endpoints). It is publicly reachable and returns operational/PHI-like data including patient_count and an ops_memo referencing renewal risk, payment flags and owner contact details, exposing sensitive information to any caller.

patient_return_lane_145 passes user-controlled input (request.GET/POST 'lane') directly to redirect(lane) without validating that it is a safe internal path. An attacker can supply an absolute URL such as https://evil.example to redirect victims to an attacker-controlled site (open redirect).

patient_bundle_thaw_169 calls pickle.loads(raw) on request body (optionally base64-decoded) coming directly from the client. pickle.loads on untrusted input is a well-known remote code execution vector because the attacker can craft a payload that executes arbitrary code during deserialization.

patient_workset_rebind_193 builds a workset with security-sensitive defaults (role=viewer, approved=False, balance=0) then calls workset.update(payload) where payload is the full user-supplied JSON body. A caller can override role, tier, approved and balance, a mass-assignment / improper attribute modification flaw that breaks authorization assumptions.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Instance Attributes

extra.message: patient_formula_cast_251 calls eval(expr, {'__builtins__': {}}, ...) where expr is taken directly from request.GET. The restricted builtins sandbox is escapable via class introspection (e.g. ().__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()), so this allows arbitrary Python code execution / remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code

extra.message: patient_crumb_lane_289 sets a cookie via response.set_cookie('portal_crumb', marker) where marker is the raw request.GET value, and the cookie is set without Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite attributes. This reflects user input into a cookie and ships an insecurely-configured cookie.

patient_identity_ping_335 performs a queue action and accepts arbitrary handle/channel inputs but has no authentication and no _wrk_gate check, unlike the other ops endpoints. Any unauthenticated caller can invoke it, a missing-authorization flaw.

patient_identity_hint_362 authenticates callers against a hardcoded verifier table known = {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'} embedded in source. These hardcoded credentials act as a static backdoor: anyone who reads the code (or guesses) can pass the check and bypass intended authorization.

patient_origin_mirror_372 reflects the attacker-controlled Origin request header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This permissive CORS policy lets any malicious origin issue credentialed cross-origin requests and read the responses, enabling cross-site data theft.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: patient_jinja_cast_383 builds a Jinja2 template from user input (Template('Result: ' + fragment).render() with fragment from request.GET) without a sandboxed environment. This is server-side template injection allowing arbitrary code execution (e.g. via cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.popen).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code

extra.message: patient_shell_probe_395 calls _os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) where host comes directly from request.GET. Because the value is concatenated into a shell command string, an attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. 127.0.0.1; whoami) to execute arbitrary operating-system commands.

patient_nonce_roll_403 parses length = int(request.GET.get('length', '24')) with no upper bound and then iterates range(length) building a string of that size. A caller can supply an enormous length to drive unbounded CPU and memory consumption (denial of service).

patient_nonce_roll_403 generates a security-relevant code using the non-cryptographic random module (random.choice(alphabet) for each character) instead of secrets. random is predictable, so the resulting nonce/code is vulnerable to guessing.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: patient_mongo_lane_412 passes a user-controlled JSON document straight to MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query) where query = payload.get('filter', payload). An attacker can supply MongoDB operators such as $ne, $where or $gt to alter the query logic, exfiltrate records or execute JavaScript via $where (NoSQL injection).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: patient_frame_slip_422 explicitly disables browser protections by setting X-XSS-Protection: 0 and an empty Content-Security-Policy header on the response, weakening the default security posture and enabling clickjacking/XSS that the headers would otherwise mitigate.

patient_trust_drift_432 creates ssl._create_unverified_context() and passes it to urllib.request.urlopen(...). This disables TLS certificate validation, allowing a network attacker to impersonate the partner endpoint via man-in-the-middle and intercept or tamper with the request.

patient_trace_panel_442 returns sensitive deployment details in the response, including os.environ.get('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE') and the absolute BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path. Exposing the settings module and internal directory layout aids further attacks.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: patient_xml_fold_453 parses untrusted request.body with lxml etree.fromstring using a parser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True and no_network=False. External/general entity resolution is enabled, so an attacker can use crafted XML with external entities to read local files, trigger SSRF, or cause denial of service (XXE).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded value 'dev-secret-change-me-only-for-local-use' when the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is unset. A known SECRET_KEY allows an attacker to forge session cookies and CSRF tokens, defeating authentication and CSRF protections if this fallback is ever used in a deployed environment.

DEBUG defaults to True (env_bool('DJANGO_DEBUG', True)). If the application is deployed without explicitly setting DJANGO_DEBUG=0, Django debug mode remains enabled, leaking detailed stack traces, settings and source paths to users on errors.
